disclaimer: A negotiation aid, not financial, legal, or tax advice. Multipliers and scripts reflect reported 2026 third-party benchmarks and ranges — never quotes, promises, or platform rules.

negotiation_scripts.body: Hi {{brand}} team — thanks for the offer. Based on my last-10-video average of {{views_avg}} views, my {{deliverable}} slots benchmark at ${{range_lo}}–${{range_hi}} on the 2026 creator rate card for my tier. My counter is ${{counter}} for the post fee alone. I can flex on scope or timeline, but the rate is the rate — it's what the numbers support.
negotiation_scripts.grounded_in: Rate card: quote at the top of the range — creators list rates ~23% above what they accept.
negotiation_scripts.tip: Quote high and expect to be negotiated down ~23%. The counter names the benchmark, not your feelings.
negotiation_scripts.title: Lowball counter
negotiation_scripts.when: The offer came in under your tier range.

negotiation_scripts.body: Quick flag on the usage terms, {{brand}}: the post fee covers organic placement only. Paid-ad usage is priced separately, per the 2026 benchmarks: {{usage_tier_label}}. That's a ${{usage_addon}} line item on top of the ${{post_fee}} post fee, with a hard end date in the contract. Running my content as your ads for a year captures thousands in value for you — it has to be its own line.
negotiation_scripts.grounded_in: Rate card: paid-ad usage is +50–100% as a separate line item — the single most-neglected line item in creator deals.
negotiation_scripts.tip: Never let paid-ad usage hide inside the post fee. Name the tier, name the multiplier, name the end date.
negotiation_scripts.title: Usage-rights upsell
negotiation_scripts.when: The contract asks for paid-ad usage priced inside the post fee.

negotiation_scripts.body: On exclusivity, {{brand}} — a broad category lock for {{exclusivity_term}} would freeze out other sponsor revenue for me, so I can't sign it as written. I can do named competitors for 30 days at +25% (${{exclusivity_fee}}) or 60–90 days at +50%, with the competitor list written into the contract. If you need the full category for 6+ months, the premium has to actually cover the deals I'd lose.
negotiation_scripts.grounded_in: Rate card levers: 30-day exclusivity +25%, 60–90 days +50%; broad 6+ month category locks need a premium that covers lost deals.
negotiation_scripts.tip: Narrow exclusivity to named competitors, put a number on it, or don't sign it.
negotiation_scripts.title: Exclusivity pushback
negotiation_scripts.when: The deal wants broad or long exclusivity without paying for it.

negotiation_scripts.body: I can hit a {{turnaround}} turnaround, {{brand}} — but it means dropping scheduled work and reordering my content calendar, so rush delivery carries a {{rush_percent}}% rush fee on the post fee. If the timeline can move to {{standard_turnaround}}, the standard rate applies. Your call either way.
negotiation_scripts.grounded_in: No research benchmark exists for rush fees — this script carries a fill-in rate instead of a fake number.
negotiation_scripts.tip: Rush means dropping paid work and reordering your content calendar. Set the premium; don't apologize for it.
negotiation_scripts.title: Rush-fee ask
negotiation_scripts.when: The brand wants a 48–72 hour turnaround on your normal timeline.

red_flags.detail: Unlimited, forever paid-ad rights bundled into the post fee. This turns your post into the brand's permanent ad creative for the price of one post.
red_flags.fix: Price perpetual usage as its own line item — or refuse outright. Never fold it into the post fee.
red_flags.title: Perpetual usage for organic price

red_flags.detail: Net-90 means you are financing the brand's marketing for a quarter. Without escrow, you have no leverage if they ghost.
red_flags.fix: Counter net-30 and 50% upfront — mandatory for any brand you haven't worked with.
red_flags.title: Net-90+ payment with no escrow

red_flags.detail: An open revision clause is a blank check on your time. 'Just one more tweak' becomes a second production cycle you don't get paid for.
red_flags.fix: Cap revisions in writing: two rounds included, paid rate per additional round.
red_flags.title: Unlimited revisions

red_flags.detail: If they can cancel after you've filmed and owe you nothing, all the production risk sits on you.
red_flags.fix: Kill fee in writing: a fixed percentage of the fee if they cancel after filming starts.
red_flags.title: No kill fee after filming

red_flags.detail: Indefinite ad spend off your account and face. Whitelisting is always a premium, always monthly, always revocable.
red_flags.fix: Price it monthly, separately from the post fee. Set a hard end date and keep kill-switch access.
red_flags.title: Perpetual whitelisting

red_flags.detail: A category lock kills other sponsor revenue for half a year. One clause can cost you more than the deal pays.
red_flags.fix: Narrow to named competitors, or demand a premium that actually covers the lost deals.
red_flags.title: Broad / category exclusivity, 6+ months

scoring.note: The checklist scores the deal's contract structure — not its pay, which the Deal Tracker benchmarks separately against the rate card.
rules: Any 'walk_away' flag checked → verdict: walk away. The structure is hostile no matter the price.
Otherwise score = 2 points per 'major' flag, 1 per 'minor'.
Score 0 → clean: proceed, price the post. Score 1–2 → caution: fix the flagged terms before signing. Score 3+ → walk away.

source: Wave 15 — The Deal Room. Usage-rights multipliers come from the wave-2 2026 sponsorship research pass (usage rights +50–100% band) and the 2026 rate card chapter; scripts are grounded in the rate-card negotiation rules. Wave 22 added 3 pitch email templates (from the sponsorship-pitch skill's outreach procedure) and 10 contract red-flag items (from the Deal Room negotiation content and the deal-negotiation skill) plus contract scoring rules.

usage_rights_tiers.basis: Definitional: the base post fee covers organic placement only. Not a market rate — it's the absence of a line item.
usage_rights_tiers.description: Content lives on your channel. No paid amplification, no re-runs as ads.
usage_rights_tiers.label: Organic only

usage_rights_tiers.basis: Reported +50% — takes the bottom of the wave-2 2026 research band for paid-ad usage (+50–100% on top of the post fee).
usage_rights_tiers.description: Brand re-runs your content as paid ads for one month.
usage_rights_tiers.label: Paid ads, 30 days

usage_rights_tiers.basis: Reported +75% — the midpoint of the wave-2 2026 research band for paid-ad usage (+50–100%).
usage_rights_tiers.description: Brand re-runs your content as paid ads for half a year.
usage_rights_tiers.label: Paid ads, 6 months

usage_rights_tiers.basis: Reported +100% — the top of the wave-2 2026 research band for paid-ad usage (+50–100%). Cap the end date in writing.
usage_rights_tiers.description: Brand re-runs your content as paid ads for a full year.
usage_rights_tiers.label: Paid ads, 12 months

usage_rights_tiers.basis: Creator surveys report whitelisting as a premium on top of paid-ad usage, but no research-backed multiplier exists. Quote your own monthly rate, keep it a separate line item, and keep kill-switch access.
usage_rights_tiers.description: Brand runs paid ads through your handle. Always monthly, always revocable.
usage_rights_tiers.label: Whitelisting — ads run from YOUR account

usage_rights_tiers.basis: No safe multiplier exists for a perpetual buyout. Price it as its own line item — never fold it into the post fee — or refuse outright. 2.0× is shown as a negotiation floor, never a rate.
usage_rights_tiers.description: Brand owns the content outright in perpetuity.
usage_rights_tiers.label: Full buyout — all rights, all media, forever

pitch_templates.title: Cold pitch (first outreach)
pitch_templates.when: First email to a brand that has never heard of you. One targeted email per brand — never bulk blasts.
pitch_templates.subject: [Channel Name] x [Brand] — a 60-second integration idea
pitch_templates.body:
Hi [Contact Name] —

I'm [Your Name], I make [Niche] videos for [Audience Size] [Audience Descriptor]. My last 10 videos averaged [Avg Views] views ([Top Geography] audience).

Idea for [Brand]: [One specific integration concept tied to THEIR product — the thing their ads can't show]. I'd do it as [Deliverable] at [Rate].

Worth a 15-minute call this week? If it's not a fit, no reply needed.

[Your Name]
[Channel link]
placeholders: One specific integration concept tied to THEIR product — the thing their ads can't show
pitch_templates.grounded_in: sponsorship-pitch skill: under 120 words; subject '[Channel] x [Brand] — 60-second integration idea'; one line who you are, one line of numbers, one specific concept, your rate, one call to action. Never 'dear partnerships team' — address the human.
pitch_templates.honesty_note: Fill every [bracket] with YOUR real numbers — never invent or inflate stats. Sponsors verify; one caught lie ends the relationship.

pitch_templates.title: The one follow-up (7 days later)
pitch_templates.when: Exactly one nudge, 7 days after the cold pitch got no reply. Then move on — a second nudge is spam.
pitch_templates.subject: Re: [Channel Name] x [Brand] — one line
pitch_templates.body:
Hi [Contact Name] — one quick bump on my note from last week: [One-sentence reminder of the integration idea] for [Brand].

If the timing's off, no reply needed — I won't write again. If it's interesting, I'm holding [Deliverable] slots for [Month].

[Your Name]
placeholders: One-sentence reminder of the integration idea
pitch_templates.grounded_in: sponsorship-pitch skill: follow up exactly once — then move on. ~5% reply rate is normal; the system works on volume, not on chasing.
pitch_templates.honesty_note: Permission-based outreach only. 'No reply needed — I won't write again' is the line that keeps one nudge from becoming harassment.

pitch_templates.title: Warm intro (referral or mutual connection)
pitch_templates.when: Someone they trust pointed you at each other — name the connection in the first line.
pitch_templates.subject: [Mutual Connection] suggested I reach out — [Channel Name] x [Brand]
pitch_templates.body:
Hi [Contact Name] — [Mutual Connection] ([Their role / how you know them]) suggested we talk.

I'm [Your Name], I make [Niche] videos for [Audience Size] [Audience Descriptor] ([Avg Views] average views on my last 10). [Mutual Connection] thought [Brand]'s [Their Product] would land with them because [One-line reason].

Idea: [One specific integration concept]. [Deliverable] at [Rate].

Open to a quick intro call? [Mutual Connection] said you're the right person — happy to loop them in.

[Your Name]
placeholders: Their role / how you know them
pitch_templates.grounded_in: sponsorship-pitch skill: find the human, name the connection first, keep it under 120 words, one specific concept, one call to action.
pitch_templates.honesty_note: Only use this template when the connection is real and has agreed to be named. A fake 'mutual friend' is a lie that travels.

contract_flags.title: Full copyright / IP assignment for a sponsored-post fee
contract_flags.detail: The contract transfers OWNERSHIP of the content (a copyright assignment), not a license. For one post fee you lose the right to repost, repurpose, or ever use your own work again — and the brand can resell it.
contract_flags.fix: License, never assign: name the exact usage window (e.g. paid ads, 12 months) with a hard end date, priced as its own line item. IP assignment is a buyout of your catalogue — it needs buyout money or a refusal.

contract_flags.title: Brand can cancel anytime — you can't
contract_flags.detail: Termination-for-convenience belongs to the brand alone. They can kill the deal after you've filmed and owe you nothing, while you're locked in for the full term.
contract_flags.fix: Mutual termination rights, and a kill fee in writing: a fixed percentage of the fee if they cancel after filming starts. All production risk must not sit on you.

contract_flags.title: Vague usage grant — 'all media now known or hereafter devised'
contract_flags.detail: An open-ended usage clause lets the brand run your face on billboards, TV, and packaging years from now — media you never priced — because the grant was written to cover everything.
contract_flags.fix: Name the media (organic post? paid social? which platforms?), the window (30 days / 6 months / 12 months), and any spend cap — in writing, with an end date.

contract_flags.title: Exclusivity that auto-renews
contract_flags.detail: A 60-day exclusivity that silently renews unless you opt out is a 6-month category lock wearing a 60-day costume. One clause quietly freezes out half a year of sponsor revenue.
contract_flags.fix: Fixed term, written end date, no auto-renewal. Any extension is a new negotiation with new money — priced at the exclusivity premium (+25% for 30 days, +50% for 60–90).

contract_flags.title: Pay tied to guaranteed views (clawback clauses)
contract_flags.detail: The fee shrinks — or must be repaid — if the video misses a view threshold. You don't control the algorithm, the feed, or the brand's own boosting, so a guarantee prices in risk you can't manage.
contract_flags.fix: Flat fee for the deliverable. Performance bonuses are fine as UPSIDE (extra pay if it pops), never as the base with a clawback.

contract_flags.title: One-sided morality clause
contract_flags.detail: The brand can terminate for anything it deems reputationally harmful — your old posts, your opinions, your other sponsors — while no equivalent standard binds them.
contract_flags.fix: Mutual, narrowly defined (conviction-level conduct, not vibes), with a written cure period so one bad tweet doesn't vaporize the fee.

contract_flags.title: No written payment schedule or invoicing terms
contract_flags.detail: 'We'll sort payment after launch' is how net-90-by-default happens. Without written terms you have no leverage when the invoice goes quiet.
contract_flags.fix: 50% upfront for any brand you haven't worked with, balance on delivery, net-30, and a late fee — all in the contract, not in the email thread.

contract_flags.title: Vague 'brand approval' with no rounds or timeline
contract_flags.detail: An open approval clause is unlimited revisions wearing a nicer suit: 'just one more tweak' becomes a second production cycle you don't get paid for, on their schedule.
contract_flags.fix: Two approval rounds included, a 5-business-day review clock, and silence-is-approval in writing. Paid rate per round beyond two.

contract_flags.title: No FTC disclosure language in the contract
contract_flags.detail: If the contract never mentions disclosure, the compliance risk quietly sits on you — and FTC fines land on the creator, not the brand's legal team. In 2026 the FTC is targeting individual creators for disclosure violations at scale (fines cited up to ~$53K per violation — the exact figure is uncertain across sources).
contract_flags.fix: A disclosure clause both sides sign: clear #ad / 'paid partnership' labeling, and you keep final say on where the disclosure sits in the content. AI-generated content needs its own disclosure too in 2026.

contract_flags.title: Deliverables described as 'and related content'
contract_flags.detail: 'One video and related content' quietly expands into a cutdown, a Story set, and a pinned comment campaign — three deliverables for the price of one.
contract_flags.fix: Exact deliverable list: format, length, platform, posting date. Anything beyond the list is a new line item with a new price.

contract_scoring.note: Scores the CONTRACT's structure — not the pay (the rate calculator benchmarks that) and not the offer terms (the Deal Room red-flag checklist covers those). A negotiation aid, NOT legal advice: contracts above $500 deserve a real lawyer's eyes.
rules: Any 'walk_away' flag checked → verdict: don't sign as written. The structure is hostile no matter the price.
Otherwise score = 2 points per 'major' flag, 1 per 'minor'.
Score 0 → clean: the contract structure reads fine — price the post next.
Score 1–2 → caution: fix the flagged terms in writing before you sign.
Score 3+ → don't sign as written: the flagged terms stack up to a deal that costs you more than it pays.
